title: Bike Dino: Mill Road
subtitle: Parkside to Brooks Road. Potholes included
intro: Space or Up to jump (hold for higher), Down to duck
introTouch: Tap to jump, hold for higher
restart: Space, click or tap to ride again
lightsOn: Sunset. Lights on: white at the front, red at the back. That is GBP50 you did not pay.

landmarks.name: Arjuna Wholefoods
landmarks.fact: Arjuna Wholefoods on Mill Road is good, if often pricey, for vegan and special diets.

landmarks.name: Mill Road Cemetery
landmarks.fact: Mill Road Cemetery: quieter than the road, and far fewer potholes.

landmarks.name: Gwydir Street
landmarks.fact: Mill Road has very well-stocked Chinese, Korean, South Asian and Middle-Eastern supermarkets.

landmarks.name: Cycle King
landmarks.fact: Cycle King, 195-197 Mill Rd: brand new bikes of reasonable quality for around GBP130.

landmarks.name: Mill Road Bridge
landmarks.fact: Mill Road Bridge takes you over the railway into Romsey.

landmarks.name: Bike Shed / Cam Cycles
landmarks.fact: The Bike Shed and Cam Cycles on Mill Road sell parts and bikes.

landmarks.name: Romsey
landmarks.fact: Cheaper new bikes of good quality are found away from the centre, e.g. Mill Road.

landmarks.name: Brooks Road
landmarks.fact: End of Mill Road. College is 2.5 km back the other way. Sidney Street is one-way.

facts: After sunset your bike must have lights: white at the front, red at the back. No lights is a GBP50 fine.
Red lanes are cycle lanes. Cycling on the pavement is illegal and discourteous.
Register your bike with the Porters to use the secure bike shed in Forecourt.
Lock the frame to something solid. U-locks are a particularly good choice.
Bike theft is one of Cambridge's biggest industries, especially at the start of the year.
Sidney Street is one-way. Cycle the wrong way and you may be fined.
A bell is extremely useful in Cambridge. Use it politely.
Obey Cyclists Dismount signs. They usually mean a bridge or a crowd ahead.
A good used bike costs GBP100 or more, a new one GBP200 to 300.
College contents insurance now covers pedal cycles and accessories.
Swap quick-release wheels for nuts and bolts. In Cambridge they are an invitation to theft.
Helmets are not compulsory, but a decent one from Decathlon is a good investment.
The SBR Environment Officer works with College on green policies and upcycling events.
The SBR room at I2, First Court was at one time a bicycle room.
The Samuel Butler Room was founded in 1960.

pothole: Swallowed by a Mill Road pothole. It has its own postcode.
Pothole. The council has been informed. Repeatedly.
scooter: Tripped over an abandoned Lime scooter. It was parked responsibly, apparently.
cones: Cone collected. Please return it to the roadworks.
You hit a traffic cone. It has a better helmet than you.
roadworks: Roadworks. They have been there since before you matriculated.
busstop: Rode into the bus stop queue. The Citi 2 is still not here.
The queue for the bus has absorbed you. You live here now.
pigeons: Pigeon strike. They had right of way.
Ambushed by Mill Road pigeons. They were after your sandwich.
